column15: Brief's own calibration brand for "light". Cited article confirms Double Black was created by "adding more peaty malt whiskies" to Black Label, i.e. Black already carries a peaty component. This batch's samples are mostly Red Label (the lighter end of the light band).
Independent bottler. Distillery rows added below for Girvan/Royal Brackla/Dalmore/Tomatin/BenRiach, named in this brand's samples.

Blended Scotch produced by Inver House Distillers (ThaiBev subsidiary). Inver House's own malt distilleries (Balmenach, Pulteney, Knockdhu, Speyburn) are not notably peated, so the blend is inferred unpeated; no source states this directly for the blend itself.
Core range (10/12/14/16/21yo, vintages) is unpeated. The distillery separately bottles a "Peaty Tang" expression (see rule) and the much heavier Old Ballantruan, which is not in this batch's samples.

Core range is Speyside's classic lightly-peated house style (brief's own calibration example). Peat Smoke is a separate heavily-peated bottling in the distillery's own lineup, see rule (matches brief's own worked example verbatim).

Historic Belfast brand revived by Echlinville Distillery (Co. Down, Northern Ireland; coded IE because the Irish Whiskey GI covers the whole island). Core range (PX, 1808, Oloroso, Blend) is unpeated Irish-style, BUT the cited Wikipedia Irish-whiskey article names "Dunville's peated" as a specific, named exception to the Irish norm. This batch's "Dunville's Dead Island" sample may or may not be that peated release -- could not confirm either way this session, reviewer should check before trusting the base peatProfile for that particular bottling.
Blended Scotch sold under Whyte & Mackay. No peat-specific source found; inferred unpeated from the company's typical portfolio character (Dalmore/Fettercairn/Jura are not notably smoky).

Confirmed independent bottler of vintage single malts, grains and blended malts. Distillery rows added below for Mortlach/Macallan/Bunnahabhain/Caol Ila/Bowmore/Laphroaig/North British, all named in this brand's samples.

Independent bottler (A. Dewar Rattray). Distillery rows added below for Glenrothes/Auchentoshan, named in this brand's samples. Also markets its own recreated blended-malt brand "Stronachie" (see stronachie row), named after a long-closed distillery not in the Wikipedia operating-distilleries authority file.

Colorado craft distillery; its own site states "American Single Malt Whiskey" as its focus, with no bourbon mentioned. Core range presumed unpeated; catalogue also lists "Boulder Peated Malt" as a distinct expression -- likely already caught by the central "peated" keyword rule, no producer rule added. defaultTypeName left empty since it is unclear whether the whole range is single malt only.

Islay single malt brand (Morrison & Mackay / Morrison Scotch Whisky Distillers); source distillery undisclosed. This batch's own samples say "Peated" and "Lightly Peated" for the Flora range, strongly suggesting the whole brand is peated Islay malt, but no accessible citation was found this session (official domain is parked, retailer pages 403, no Wikipedia article, Wikipedia search returned nothing relevant) so peat is left unknown rather than guessed. Reviewer should very likely set this to light/medium/heavy after checking the brand's own materials -- CLAUDE.md's own flavor_rule documentation already cites "Mac-Talla Flora Lightly Peated" as a case the central peated/lightly-peated keyword priority ordering is designed to handle, so no producer-specific rule was added here either.

Core range is commonly understood to be unpeated, but no source found this session states that explicitly, so left unknown rather than guessed. Catalogue also lists "Ben Nevis Traditional Peated Malt" -- likely already caught by the central "peated" keyword rule, no producer rule added.

No web presence found (official site, Wikipedia). "Glen-" naming convention suggests an own-label Scotch blend/vatting, common for private retail labels. Also appears inside a "Slaur Sardet Glen Scanlan" sample (see slaur-sardet row); relationship between the two brand strings is unclear.

Own blended-Scotch brand of Tomatin Distillery Co (alongside Talisman). Tomatin's own house style is one of the least-peated Highland malts, so the blend is inferred unpeated; no source found stating this directly for Antiquary itself.

Mitchell & Son (historic Dublin wine/spirit merchant); bottles the "Spot" family (Green/Yellow/Blue/Red Spot) pure pot still Irish whiskey sourced from Midleton. Modeled as kind=bottler per brief's rule, so peat is left unknown even though pot still Irish whiskey of this style is conventionally unpeated.

Confirmed blended malt Lowland Scotch whisky, explicitly described by Douglas Laing as unpeated ("a marriage of Single Malts from Scotland's Lowlands"). bottlerSlug=douglas-laing is not defined in this batch's own producer.tsv -- Douglas Laing is named directly in the brief's own kind=bottler examples, so another batch will almost certainly define it.

Confirmed as the single-cask independent-bottler range of The Vintage Malt Whisky Company (Glasgow, est. 1992 by Brian Crook). Distillery rows added below for Dailuaine/Inchgower/Strathisla, named in this brand's samples.
Springbank's heavily-peated, double-distilled sibling brand (named directly in the brief's own sibling-pair list). Cited article: "Longrow Single Malt is a highly peated, double-distilled whisky".
No web presence found this session; country and style could not be identified.

French single malt, distilled in Cognac from estate-grown heirloom barley (founder Allison Parc). Official site markets it as smooth and approachable but states no peat/smoke information either way, so left unknown rather than assumed.
No web presence found this session ("Double Cask"/"Triple Cask" samples only, a naming convention many brands use); country and style could not be identified.

Bob Dylan's American whiskey brand: Kentucky Straight Bourbon (Ascension, Revival/Tennessee Straight Bourbon), Straight Rye (Refuge), and Double Barrel (Revelation), produced with Six Mile Creek Distillery (Ken Pierce, master distiller). No peated expression found on site; defaultTypeName left empty since the range spans bourbon, rye and Tennessee whiskey.

This batch's own sample pairs it directly with the distillery ("Bladnoch Kirkcowan"). Bladnoch's current site (checked this session) no longer lists Kirkcowan, likely a discontinued release from an earlier ownership era (pre-David Prior). No peat citation found.
No web presence found this session; apostrophe-surname styling suggests an Irish-themed own-label, unconfirmed.

No web presence found this session. One of its own two sample names is "Slaur Sardet Glen Scanlan" (see glen-scanlan row) -- possibly an importer/retailer label bundling other own-brand whiskies rather than a single coherent brand; unconfirmed.
Confirmed: Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey distributed exclusively by Hood River Distillers, aged in new charred oak.

One of the very few peated Lowland distilleries; cited article: "Ailsa Bay and Annandale have become characterised by their use of peat, with a flavor profile more typical of Islay whisky." Exact ordinal is uncertain -- some releases are reported elsewhere as very lightly peated (~1.2ppm "Sweet Smoke"), others heavier for blending stock, so treat "medium" as approximate and verify against the specific expression actually in stock.

Believed (general knowledge, not confirmed this session) to be a Bladnoch-associated blended Scotch from an earlier ownership era; the current Bladnoch site does not list it and no other citation was found.
No web presence found this session; "Dram"/"Loch" naming strongly suggests an own-label Scotch blend.
No web presence found this session; "Glen-" naming suggests an own-label Scotch blend.

Confirmed blending/bottling company ("Blenders and Bottlers of the Finest Scotch Whiskies"; ranges include Old Malt Cask, The Sovereign, Hepburn's Choice, The First Editions). Distillery row added below for Tullibardine, named in this brand's sample. Hunter Laing also owns Ardnahoe distillery (peated Islay malt), not added here since it is not named in this batch's sample.
Catalogue spells the brand simply "Koriyama"; the operating distillery's formal name is Asaka Distillery, in Kōriyama, Fukushima Prefecture, founded 2016. No peat information found.

No web presence confirmed this session (domain did not resolve, no Wikipedia article). Apostrophe-surname naming matches an independent-bottler range convention. A possible link to Aberko Ltd's "McGibbon's" range is recalled but could not be verified online this session.
No web presence found this session; Irish-surname styling suggests an Irish whiskey own-label, unconfirmed.

Skrewball Peanut Butter Whiskey, a San Diego flavored-whiskey brand. Official site was unreachable this session (connection refused) and no Wikipedia article covers the product itself (only NASCAR sponsorship pages), so peat is left unknown rather than assumed, despite flavored American whiskey being very unlikely to be peated.

Built mainly to supply Diageo's blends; occasional single malt Special Releases since September 2023, and malt from here was used in Johnnie Walker Black Ruby (2024/2025). No peat information found -- large Diageo blending distilleries often run more than one peat level, so unpeated should not be assumed.
No web presence found this session; country and style could not be identified.

Kurayoshi distillery, Tottori Prefecture, owned by Matsui Shuzo, distilling since 2017. The range is known to include both peated and unpeated bottlings; not disambiguated by the single "Tottori" sample seen in this batch.

No web presence confirmed this session (official-looking domains either failed to resolve or served an unrelated parked/mismatched cert page, no Wikipedia article). Naming convention (surname & surname) matches an independent-bottler range.

Grain distillery; authority file lists no region for it (grain distilleries are outside the malt-region convention), lowland inferred from its South Ayrshire location. Referenced only as a Hart Brothers bottling.
Referenced only as a Hart Brothers bottling (sample says "Brackla").
Referenced only as a Hart Brothers bottling.
One of the least-peated Highland malts by reputation; also produces the Antiquary and Talisman blends. Referenced as a Hart Brothers bottling.

Referenced only as a Hart Brothers bottling. Brief's own sibling-pair list names BenRiach/Curiositas (peated) as a pair to watch; not enough was researched this session to set a base peat value confidently. A Curiositas brand row (parentSlug=benriach) may be needed if it surfaces in another batch.
Referenced only as a Murray McDavid bottling.
Referenced only as a Murray McDavid bottling.
Famously the unpeated Islay malt (per brief itself); its peated sibling Moine is not seen in this batch's samples. Referenced as a Murray McDavid bottling.
Well-known heavily-peated Islay malt, a major component of many blends (incl. Johnnie Walker). Referenced as a Murray McDavid bottling.
Per brief's own calibration list (medium). Referenced as a Murray McDavid bottling.
Per brief's own calibration list (heavy). Referenced as a Murray McDavid bottling.

Grain distillery, Edinburgh, founded 1885. Region left empty (grain, no malt-region classification) but legalRegion set to lowland since it is physically in Edinburgh. Referenced only as a component of a Murray McDavid vatting ("Air Leth").
Referenced only as a Dewar Rattray bottling.
Lowland malt, traditionally unpeated; also one of the few triple-distilled Scotch malts. Referenced as a Dewar Rattray bottling.
Referenced only as a Cooper's Choice bottling.
Referenced only as a Cooper's Choice bottling.
Referenced only as a Cooper's Choice bottling (via The Vintage Malt Whisky Co).
Referenced only as a Hunter Laing (Old & Rare) bottling.

Parent of Longrow (heavy) and Hazelburn (unpeated, not in this batch). Core Springbank itself is medium-peated per the distillery's own process (6h peat smoke + 30h hot air, "medium-peated" per the cited article).

Northern Ireland distillery (Co. Down, est. 2013, the first new Northern Irish distillery in generations), custodian of the Dunville's brand. Coded IE since the Irish Whiskey GI covers the whole island of Ireland; physically located in the UK (Northern Ireland).
Dewar Rattray's own recreated blended-malt brand, named after a long-closed distillery not present in the Wikipedia operating-distilleries authority file; no further citation found this session.
